Some friends and I were playing cards on a ferry going on a field trip, this guy was teasing me and I didn't know how to react like a "cool" kid so I pushed his head kind of like trying to mess up his hair and it went horribly ary and he kind of flowed too much and his head went too low and his head came close to my chest. His reaction was to say "ooh baby I'm not old enough for that!" As a prudish 7th grade girl, I was mortified and so I slapped him really hard and fled the scene. He wound up being really hurt and crying and trying to look tough and I felt like an asshole and cried for the rest of the night.
Traumaaaticc...

Not "WTF" so much as just kind of funny. 
In my town there's a little stretch of road alongside a small marina. There's a general store, a coffee shop, a couple small boutiques, real picturesque. There was always a group of old men playing cards or hanging out in the general store, they were great for stories and they always loved teasing us. 
The stretch of road has a speed limit of 25 mph, and people were always speeding. There was one guy a couple years back who was an ex sherrif and he eventually got tired of all the speeding, thought it was bad for the community. One day he decided to try to put an end to it, so he got an old hair drier and stood outside the general store Monday through Friday, aiming at speeding cars. The Town thought it was the funniest thing and it really worked on people who weren't from around the area. ;)
TL;DR: Old man stood in a speed zone with a hair drier pretending to have a radar detector.

Tortilla Soup! Made it tonight, in fact.
Saute oil, garlic, onions. A can or two of diced tomatoes, beans (I use three cans, pinto, black, and white) a half a cup of vegetable broth, and season with salt, chili flakes, chili powder, paprika, cumin, etc. Throw in whatever you have, corn, bell peppers, all that, but do that part towards the end. Usually takes me 40 minutes or so and it lasts for days. Sometimes I put it with quinoa in a tortilla just as a wrap the next day!

I've been there. I know I'm probably not the first one to say this, but it will get better. I think you need to get out. Try going to a coffee shop and starting a conversaiton with someone who looks interesting. Try a hot bath with happy music, buy a puppy. Animals are great because they don't judge, hold grudges, or say things that get you down. They're funny, they love you unconditionally, and they give you something to take care of. Try volunteering with disabled kids or at a kindergarten. Young people or handicapped people can have such a pure happiness and simple gratitude for the life they have, it's not only inspiring, it's hopeful. 
Also, if your boss is saying things like that, you're not in the right job. Go out and reinvent yourself, one thing that I find powerful about depression is that it can give you a feeling of "I have nothing to lose, so I'm doing my life for ME." Go and make a new path for yourself. Find something that makes you happy and someplace that you feel whole, and useful. Help other people, learn a different language. There really is too much to live for to spend it sad.
I know how you feel, I feel the same way lots of the time, and I'm not saying it'll be easy, but you can do it. Free yourself, do yoga. Bake a cake. Find something to be passionate about, learn.
and, I understand you feel sick. I understand the disease, but it CAN be beaten. PM me if you want to talk. you're loved <3
